about: The page's words in each shipped language (D-394): how the page speaks to the player (voice), and the game's terms as the players of tabletop role-playing games in that language say them (terms: the English term, the other English forms it takes in the phrases, what it means on the page, and its word in each language). test/i18n/translate.ts gives the translator a language's voice and the terms of each batch. The Italian follows it.json, which is curated. unsure: the choices to check with a player of that language. Not shipped: it serves the command, not the page.

voice.ar: Modern Standard Arabic, plain and short. Buttons and labels as verbal nouns (حفظ، إلغاء، إرسال) rather than imperatives; sentences speak to the player in the second person singular, masculine as Arabic software does where no neutral form exists.
voice.cs: Informal ty (tykání), as Czech games speak to the player. Buttons and labels in the infinitive or as nouns (Uložit, Zrušit). Avoid past tenses that mark the player's gender (udělal/udělala).
voice.da: Informal du. Buttons in the imperative, short (Gem, Annuller).
voice.de: Informal du, lowercase. Buttons and labels in the infinitive or as nouns (Speichern, Abbrechen), as German software does. Gender-neutral nouns where they read naturally (die Spielleitung).
voice.el: Informal singular εσύ. Buttons as nouns or singular imperatives (Αποθήκευση, Ακύρωση). Avoid forms that mark the player's gender.
voice.es: Informal tú, in a neutral Spanish read alike in Spain and Latin America: never vos or vosotros, and no word only one side uses (equipo, not ordenador or computadora). Buttons in the infinitive (Guardar, Cancelar).
voice.fi: Informal sinä, left out where Finnish allows. Buttons in the imperative or as nouns (Tallenna, Peruuta).
voice.fr: Informal tu. Buttons in the infinitive (Enregistrer, Annuler). A non-breaking space (U+00A0) before : ; ? ! as French typography wants.
voice.he: Buttons and labels as nouns or infinitives (שמירה, ביטול, לשלוח), which do not mark gender; sentences speak to the player avoiding forms that mark gender where Hebrew allows (infinitive, impersonal), masculine singular otherwise, as Hebrew software does. No niqqud.
voice.hi: Everyday Hindi in Devanagari with the respectful आप in every phrase (never तुम or its imperatives such as छुओ, but छुएँ), as Hindi apps speak; the English game words players use (रोल, मॉडिफ़ायर, सेव) in Devanagari where a Hindi word would sound bookish.
voice.hu: Informal te (tegezés), as Hungarian games speak. Buttons short, as nouns or imperatives (Mentés, Mégse).
voice.is: Informal þú. Buttons short, as nouns or imperatives (Vista, Hætta við).
voice.ja: No pronoun for the player where the sentence stands without one (avoid あなた). Buttons, labels, values and options in plain form, as nouns or dictionary forms (保存, 閉じる, セーブに戻る). Every full sentence (messages, explanations, confirmations, questions) in です/ます: 〜しますか？, 〜できます。 Full-width punctuation: 、。：？！（）.
voice.ko: Sentences in 해요체, as Korean apps and games speak (저장했어요, 다시 시도해 주세요); buttons and labels as nouns (저장, 취소). No pronoun for the player (never 당신).
voice.nb: Bokmål, informal du. Buttons in the imperative (Lagre, Avbryt).
voice.nl: Informal je/jij. Buttons in the infinitive (Opslaan, Annuleren).
voice.pl: Informal ty. Buttons in the imperative (Zapisz, Anuluj). Avoid past tenses that mark the player's gender (zrobiłeś/zrobiłaś): present or impersonal forms.
voice.pt: Brazilian Portuguese with você, as the Brazilian role-playing community speaks (salvar, tela, rodada, sua vez); never tu or European forms (gravar, ecrã, ronda). Buttons in the infinitive (Salvar, Cancelar).
voice.ro: Informal tu. Buttons in the imperative (Salvează, Anulează). Diacritics with the comma (ș, ț), never the cedilla.
voice.ru: Informal ты, as players speak at the table. Buttons in the infinitive (Сохранить, Отменить). Avoid past tenses that mark the player's gender (сделал/сделала).
voice.sv: Informal du. Buttons in the imperative (Spara, Avbryt).
voice.tr: Informal sen. Buttons as nouns or imperatives (Kaydet, İptal).
voice.uk: Informal ти. Buttons in the infinitive (Зберегти, Скасувати). Avoid past tenses that mark the player's gender.
voice.zh: Simplified Chinese as mainland players write it: 你, never 您, and no pronoun where the sentence stands without one. Buttons and labels short, two to four characters where possible (保存, 取消, 回到存档). Full-width punctuation in Chinese text: ，。：？！（）, and “” for quotes.

master.note: the game master, played by the AI in the chat: one word in every phrase, the one players of tabletop role-playing games use for whoever runs the game, in any game. The master is one: the phrases' they and them for the master are singular, so where the language has no singular they, name the master again or leave the pronoun out: never a pronoun that reads as many people
master.hi: गेम मास्टर (never मास्टर alone, which is a schoolteacher)

character.note: the player character, the one the player plays; also 'player character'

party.note: the player's character and companions, travelling together

companion.note: a character the master plays who travels with the party and acts at its side

sheet.note: the character sheet on the page: the character's numbers, abilities and gear
sheet.ja: キャラクターシート (シート in short labels)

roll.note: a throw of the dice and its result; to roll is to throw them
roll.ja: ロール (ダイスロール where it stands alone, as a title: ロール alone reads also as a role, beside ルール) / 振る (the tray's button too)

check.note: a roll the master asks for, to see whether an action succeeds against a difficulty; never a tick box or a bank cheque

free roll.note: a roll the player makes from the tray for themselves: it counts for nothing and is not logged; free as unbound, never as without cost
free roll.pl: swobodny rzut (not rzut wolny, a free kick)

dice.note: the dice, one die, from d4 to d20; the page throws them in 3D

tray.note: the dice tray on the page, where the player throws the dice

modifier.note: the number added to a roll or taken from it; Mod is its short label beside the tray
modifier.ja: 修正値 (修正 in the short label)

natural.note: the face a die shows, before any modifier: a natural 20

quest.note: a task the character takes on, with goals, listed in the journal

goal.note: one of the things a quest asks, which the character works toward

scene.note: a stretch of play in one place and time; the page's Scene shows the current one

turn.note: a creature's moment to act in a fight (your turn, the order of the turns); a round is everyone's turns once

round.note: one pass of turns in a fight, every creature acting once (Round 3); never round as a shape

combat.note: a fight, and the page's Combat, which shows it

save.note: a saved state of the game the player can go back to, made at the end of scenes or when asked: the word of video games, never a saving throw; a button that keeps settings or a note uses the usual software verb
save.ja: セーブ / セーブする (保存 for settings and notes)
save.zh: 存档, noun and verb (保存 for settings and notes)

session zero.note: the first meeting before play, where the character and the world are made with the master

note.note: the player's own note, which the master does not read unless the player shares it

journal.note: the page's Journal: the character's quests, story and notes
journal.cs: kronika (not deník, which is the character sheet)

map.note: a map of a place, or the world map

place.note: a location of the world the character knows: a town, a cave, an inn

legend.note: the legend of a map, what its signs mean: Key and Legend are the same thing, one word

mentor.note: the setting for how much the master teaches the game outside the story

limits.note: the group of settings that holds Lines and Veils, what the game leaves out: a word different from the one for lines

lines.note: the safety tool lines and veils: lines are the topics that never appear in the game; they sit in the group Limits, so a word different from that one

veils.note: the other half of lines and veils: veils are the topics that happen only off screen, without details

clock.note: a quest's progress clock, segments that fill as something comes closer, shown as 2/4: never the time of day nor a countdown

square.note: a square of a map's grid, named like E4

unsure.ar: master مدير اللعبة (also سيد اللعبة, الراوي) and clock عدّاد, a counter rather than the literal ساعة: I found no Arabic role-playing references to lean on.
unsure.cs: check ověření (Dračí Hlídka's word; zkouška is also heard), modifier oprava, session zero nulté sezení; journal kronika because Czech players call the character sheet deník.
unsure.da: check prøve, quest mission, tray terningbakke.
unsure.de: lines Linien: German tables often keep Lines & Veils in English.
unsure.el: master αφηγητής (tables also say DM, GM), check έλεγχος, session zero; ημερολόγιο is both the journal and the calendar, which the page also names.
unsure.es: round ronda, generic: Spanish D&D says asalto.
unsure.fi: check heitto, the same word as a roll (koe is possible), modifier muunnin, tray noppa-alusta, session zero nollasessio.
unsure.he: master מנחה, modifier מתאם, veils וילונות, session zero סשן אפס.
unsure.hi: all of it wants a Hindi speaker who plays: free roll मुक्त रोल; square खाना is also food (वर्ग is the other choice); lines सीमा-रेखाएँ close to limits सीमाएँ.
unsure.hu: turn kör ({name} köre) and round forduló: Hungarian tables differ.
unsure.is: nearly all of it: I found no Icelandic role-playing references; master sögumaður, check próf, turn röð, scene atriði, modifier breytir, legend skýringar.
unsure.ja: natural 出目 (D&D players also say ナチュラル20); clock クロック.
unsure.ko: master GM (마스터 is as common), session zero 세션 0, lines 금지선.
unsure.nl: check proef (Dutch tables often say check), quest missie, modifier modifier, tray dobbelbak.
unsure.pt: written in Brazilian Portuguese, as most of the file already was: players from Portugal read it, but would write tu, guardar, ronda.
unsure.ro: master maestru de joc (Romanian tables also say GM-ul, masterul), square căsuță.
unsure.ru: dice кубики: Russian D&D says кости.
unsure.tr: check kontrol, combat çatışma, modifier değiştirici.
unsure.uk: party загін (група and партія are heard too).
unsure.zh: session zero 零号团 (tables also say 0团 or 车卡); clock 进度钟; master 主持人 rather than GM, which players use as much: one only.
